accounting.basis: Two sets of numbers. MHIL consolidated (Ind AS; FY26 revenue ₹8,373 cr, Screener EBITDA ₹2,243 cr, PAT ₹1,442 cr) and the 'Network' (adds the three PHF societies: FY26 net revenue ₹10,065 cr, operating EBITDA ₹2,638 cr, PAT ₹1,631 cr). The company's KPIs and most broker estimates are on the Network basis; EPS in the accounts (₹14.83) is on the consolidated basis.
accounting.oneOffs: FY23: ₹244 cr deferred-tax gain (voluntary liquidation of subsidiaries). FY25: ₹74 cr YEIDA charge (Jaypee acquisition) as exceptional, ₹18 cr DTL gain. FY26: ~₹142 cr tax gain on the CRL-JHL amalgamation (Q2FY26 tax rate −10%), ₹48 cr exceptional (Labour Code, stamp duty).
accounting.intangibles: Goodwill ₹3,488 cr and other intangibles ₹2,518 cr at Mar-26 (consolidated), largely from the 2020 merger fair valuation and acquisitions: reported ROE (~14%) understates returns on cash invested; the company's own pre-tax ROCE excludes them (21.8% FY26 overall, ~31% for units over 4 years old excl. CWIP).
accounting.leases: Lease liabilities ₹572 cr (consolidated) and ₹589 cr (Network) at Mar-26; EBITDA is post-Ind AS 116. Rent is small for Max (mostly owned or long-term contracted hospitals), so the pre/post Ind AS gap is ~1% of EBITDA value; asset-light built-to-suit hospitals (Mohali, Thane, Dehradun) will add lease debt as they open.
accounting.workingCapital: Network DSO 95 days at Jun-26 (87 at Mar-26) on slow CGHS/PSU collections; consolidated receivables ₹1,049 cr at Mar-26 (₹776 cr a year earlier).

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Max Healthcare Institute (MHIL consolidated, ₹ crore, Screener basis). One reportable segment, so the engine runs on a single revenue-growth path and a post-Ind AS 116 EBITDA margin (rent is not in EBITDA; lease interest is in interest; lease liabilities sit in borrowings, so the model's net cash is net of leases). The company's KPIs are on the 'Network' basis (MHIL plus three Partner Healthcare Facility societies); the bed build in `businessLines` builds Network hospital revenue (beds x 365 x occupancy x ARPOB), adds Max Lab, converts gross to net revenue and takes MHIL's consolidated share; the authoring script checks it equals model revenue. Shares: Screener FY26 profit / EPS = 97.30 cr = actual 97.33 cr (no patch). Valued on EV/EBITDA, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: From the bed build below. FY27 +19%: Q1 consolidated revenue +16.7% (Network gross +16%, +20% excluding oncology) with Kalinga only from 18-May; Q2-Q4 get the rest of Max Smart (PHF, but Max earns service fees), the last ~50 Nanavati beds, Kalinga for a full year, +100 Lucknow beds and the first ~200 Gurugram beds from end-CY2026, the oncology base effect from Q3 and the ~6% insurer price revision from Sep-Oct. FY28 +18%: Gurugram ramp, Zirakpur Mohali (400) and Nagpur (100). FY29 +15%: Pitampura, Dehradun, Patparganj (PHF, end-FY29). Street (Network net revenue) FY27E +18.5% (PL) to +24% (MOSL).

businessLines._why: Network hospital gross revenue = average operational beds x 365 x occupancy x ARPOB (company definition: gross revenue excl. Max Lab ÷ OBDs). FY26 check: (₹10,538 cr gross - ₹201 cr Max Lab) ÷ ₹77,800 = 13.29 lakh OBDs = 4,790 average beds at 76% (Mar-25 4,654, Mar-26 4,966). FY27 5,540 average beds (Q1 implied 5,231; 5,379 at Jun-26 rising to ~5,950 by Mar-27), occupancy 74% (75% in Q1; Gurugram starts low), ARPOB ₹82,300 (+6%: Q1 ₹81.9k; oncology base effect, CGHS rate revision, insurer hikes, less ~2% dilution from Kalinga at ₹35k). FY28 6,250 beds, 73%, ₹86,500 (+5%); FY29 6,750 beds, 73.5%, ₹91,250 (+5.5%) — management: ARPOB grows a couple of points above inflation. Max Lab ₹240 / 285 / 335 cr (+18-20% a year; ₹58 cr in Q1FY27, +20%). Net/gross 0.952 (FY26 0.955, Q1FY27 0.951). MHIL's consolidated share of Network net revenue 0.835 / 0.84 / 0.84 (FY25 0.811, FY26 0.832, Q1FY27 0.835): it rises as owned units (Gurugram, Kalinga, Lucknow, Mohali, Nagpur) grow faster than the PHFs, offset by Max Smart's new tower sitting in a PHF.

assumptions._marginWhy: Consolidated EBITDA margin (Screener basis: after ESOP cost; post-Ind AS 116): 27.6% FY24, 26.3% FY25, 26.8% FY26 (Q2-Q4FY26: 26.9%, 26.0%, 28.3%), 25.3% in Q1FY27 (25.8% a year earlier) with ₹195 cr of Network overheads for new units. Management: no significant rise in indirect costs until Gurugram opens, so new-bed revenue drops through from Q2. FY27 26.4%: Q2-Q4 ~0.5pp above FY26's quarters, less Gurugram start-up costs; FY28 26.9%: brownfield towers mature, oncology normalised, offset by Gurugram, Zirakpur and Nagpur start-up losses; FY29 27.4%. Network equivalents are ~0.5-1pp lower (Network operating margin 26.2% in FY26). Street (Network): PL 26.6% / 26.6%, MOSL 25.4% / 26.4%, Antique ~27% by FY28.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY27 ₹2,300 cr = ₹386 cr paid for Kalinga and YPPL in Q1 + ₹1,711 cr of project outflow (company estimate for FY27) + ~₹200 cr routine capex. FY28 ₹3,010 cr = ₹2,340 cr project outflow + ₹220 cr routine + ~₹450 cr of new lease liabilities for the 400-bed built-to-suit Zirakpur, Mohali hospital (GAM estimate from Dwarka: lease liabilities rose ₹372 cr in FY25 for ~300 beds). FY29 ₹2,565 cr = ₹2,025 cr + ₹240 cr routine + ~₹300 cr of leases (Pitampura, Dehradun). Project outflow (deck, 17-Aug-2026) excludes land and the medical-college plan (~₹300 cr per college, not firmed); it includes the funding of PHF projects (Max Smart, Patparganj), which Max lends to the societies at ~9.25% — we treat it all as capex (cash-conservative; the engine has no separate loan asset). New leases are added because lease liabilities count as debt in the model.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹447 cr = 3.1% of average gross block (₹14,232 cr, which includes ~₹6,000 cr of goodwill-like merger intangibles that are barely amortised); Q1FY27 ₹132 cr (₹528 cr annualised) after Mohali, Nanavati and Lucknow capitalisation. 3.4% gives FY27E ~₹553 cr. The engine depreciates capex at once while projects sit in CWIP (₹592 cr at Mar-26).
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Zero because the engine applies the yield to net cash after borrowings and lease liabilities, which is negative (net debt ₹2,812 cr at Mar-26). Interest income is built in `otherIncome` instead.

otherIncomeBuild._why: Built from AR FY26 note 28 (consolidated other income ₹162.6 cr; ₹155.6 cr in FY25). Treasury: bank-deposit interest ₹29.6 cr (FY25 ₹53.1 cr) on ~₹690 cr average cash (4.3%); we take 4.5% on ₹600 / 500 / 450 cr of average cash as capex absorbs cash. Loans to PHFs (₹746 cr at Mar-26 to Gujarmal Modi Hospital for Max Smart, 9.25%): ₹68.6 cr in FY26; ~₹800 / 900 / 1,000 cr average loans at 9.25% as Smart and Patparganj are funded. Recurring other (₹58 cr in FY26, ₹62 cr in FY25): unwinding on long-dated receivables and deposits ~₹11 cr, write-backs of unclaimed balances ₹24-31 cr a year (we take ~₹28 cr), deferred EPCG credit, tax-refund interest and others ~₹16-18 cr: ₹55 / 56 / 57 cr. Left out as one-offs: fair-value gain on contingent consideration ₹5.1 cr, asset-sale gain, lease modification. FY27E ₹156 cr vs FY26 ₹162.6 cr and ₹166.6 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26 (before exceptional items): lower deposit interest as cash funds Kalinga and projects.

assumptions._interestLabel: Finance cost (borrowings + lease interest; gross, before interest income)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹235 cr (incl. ₹54 cr of lease interest); Q1FY27 ₹71 cr (₹284 cr annualised) after the ECB for Kalinga. Gross debt rises with ~₹7,900 cr of capex and leases over FY27-29 against ~₹7,500 cr of operating cash; interest on ~8% of average borrowings plus lease interest (~9.5%) and less capitalisation as projects complete: ₹300 / 360 / 400 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax plus minorities (the engine has no minority line). The enacted rate is 25.17%; profits of the managed facilities (silos) are not taxed at MHIL, worth ~2.4pp in FY26 (AR FY26 tax reconciliation: ₹40 cr on ₹1,676 cr PBT). FY26 underlying 22.4% (₹233 cr reported plus the ₹142 cr one-time amalgamation gain); FY25 23.5%; but Q4FY26 26.4% and Q1FY27 26.0% (MHIL). We use 24.5%, incl. ~0.3pp for minorities (41.72% of Kalinga, ~49.78% of YPPL, both small). Brokers use 20-23% on the Network, where the PHF societies pay little tax.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividends: ₹1.5 a share for FY25 (₹146 cr), ₹2 recommended for FY26 (~13% of profit).

dcf._betaWhy: Ke = 6.5% + 0.85 x 6% = 11.6%. Net debt incl. leases is ~3% of enterprise value, so WACC is ~11.4%; the engine discounts at the cost of equity, which we keep (slightly conservative). Defensive demand; regulatory and expansion risk.
dcf._tgWhy: 6%: bed density in North India is well below the WHO norm and ARPOB grows above inflation, but supply is rising fast in NCR.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~15% (FY29E) to 9% by year 15 as the ~10,000-bed network matures.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 27.5% consolidated (FY24 27.6%, FY26 26.8%): new hospitals mature, but more beds sit in lower-ARPOB cities (Lucknow, Nagpur, Bhubaneswar) and doctor costs rise.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex incl. leases falls from ~19-26% of revenue (expansion) to 9%: replacement (depreciation ~5.5% of revenue) plus growth capex for ~9% growth via brownfields.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Brownfield towers fill as fast as Smart (80% in weeks), Gurugram breaks even within a year, oncology recovers fully and insurer price revisions stick; institutional share keeps falling.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Drug-margin caps (CGHS, Supreme Court case) spread, NCR competition lifts doctor costs, Gurugram and Zirakpur ramp slowly and acquisitions dilute ARPOB.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: How the street values Max: EV/EBITDA on FY28E or 12-month-forward EBITDA (PL 30x, Anand Rathi 32x and Antique 30x on hospitals, MOSL 33x), all on Network EBITDA. We use MHIL consolidated EBITDA (Screener; post-Ind AS 116) with net debt including lease liabilities, the basis of the model, of Max's own multiple history and of the peer multiples. 30x = Max's 31.8x median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 (no trough years: forward EBITDA never fell below half its prior peak), cut by the 6.7% median de-rating of six listed hospital peers versus their five-year median EV/EBITDA on 30-Sep-2026 (Apollo, Fortis, Narayana, Medanta, Jupiter, Rainbow; KIMS and Aster left out because new-hospital losses and the 2024 GCC demerger distort their history) = 29.7x, rounded to 30x. No growth adjustment: EBITDA growth slows from 22% a year (FY23-26, with acquisitions) to ~18% (FY26-29E) while capex doubles. Bull 37.5x and bear 26x = the 75th and 25th percentiles of the same history (40.3x, 28.2x) after the same de-rating.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Cross-check on earnings. 48x = Max's 54.6x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 on EPS before one-offs (FY23 ex the ₹244 cr deferred-tax gain, FY25 ex the YEIDA charge and DTL gain, FY26 ex the ₹142 cr amalgamation tax gain and exceptional items; 55.4x on reported EPS via forwardMedian; no trough years) cut by the 12.1% median P/E de-rating of the same six peers (= 48.0x). Bull 60x, bear 42x scale with the EV/EBITDA multiples.

cover.headline: The best hospital franchise in North India, already priced as one: 4,000 new beds have to prove they earn Max's returns
cover.lead: Max runs 17 hospitals and ~6,100 beds, three-quarters of them in Delhi NCR and Mumbai, and fills them better (75% occupancy) and bills more per bed-day (₹81.9k ARPOB) than any listed peer. It is now in its biggest build-out: ~4,000 beds by FY30 for ~₹7,000 cr, after ~1,300 acquired beds in FY25. Network revenue rose 16% in Q1FY27, but returns are falling (company pre-tax ROCE 33% in FY23, 21.8% in FY26) and profit lags EBITDA as depreciation and interest arrive first. The street values Max on **EV/EBITDA on FY28E (30-33x Network EBITDA)**. We forecast consolidated EBITDA of ₹2,635 / 3,160 / 3,694 cr and EPS of ₹15.0 / 18.0 / 21.1 for FY27-29E (in line with the street on EBITDA once put on the same basis; brokers' EPS includes partner hospitals Max does not own). Applying **30x to Sep-28E EBITDA of ₹3,427 cr** (consolidated, post-Ind AS, lease liabilities in net debt) gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with HOLD.** Cross-checks: P/E ₹939, DCF ₹405. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: 2,548 operational beds in Delhi NCR at 79% occupancy; network occupancy ~75% for four years even while adding 13% more beds; Network EBITDA of ₹71.2 lakh per bed vs ₹47-58 lakh at Apollo, Fortis and Medanta (company comparison). Brownfield towers next to full hospitals fill fast: Max Smart's new beds were ~80% occupied within weeks.

arguments.h: Growth is coming, and it is mostly brownfield
arguments.p: Capacity 6,183 beds (Aug-2026) → ~10,200 by FY30 (+601, +500, +927, +1,981 a year). We model revenue +{{F.salesGrowth.0|pct}}, +{{F.salesGrowth.1|pct}}, +{{F.salesGrowth.2|pct}} (FY27-29E) from a bed-by-bed build: average operational beds 5,540 → 6,750, occupancy 73-74%, ARPOB +5-6% a year.

arguments.h: But returns and earnings lag the beds
arguments.p: Capex plus new leases of ₹2,300-3,010 cr a year exceeds operating cash in FY27-28E; net debt incl. leases rises to ~₹4,100 cr by FY29E. EPS barely moves in FY27E (₹15.0 vs ₹14.8 reported, ₹13.8 before one-offs) and grows ~15% a year to FY29E. Government payers are a drag: CGHS drug caps cut oncology from 26% to 22% of IP revenue, and the Supreme Court questioned hospital drug markups on 30-Sep-2026.

At ₹930 Max trades at 29.5x our FY28E EV/EBITDA against a 31.8x forward median since Apr-2021; peers had de-rated ~7% by 30-Sep-2026, giving 30x and {{dcf.tp|inr}}. Our DCF (₹405) is the warning: today's price needs a ~9.0% discount rate, well below our 11.6% cost of equity.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): ramp-up of the Max Smart, Nanavati-Max and Mohali towers (management: EBITDA to follow revenue "over the next couple of quarters"), the oncology base effect from Q3, the ~6% insurer price revision from Sep-Oct 2026 and whether DSO comes back from 95 days.
Phased opening of the 500-bed Gurugram greenfield from end-CY2026 (starting with ~200 beds) and its start-up losses.
The Supreme Court proceedings on hospital drug markups and any cap on trade margins; CGHS payments and rate revisions.
Kalinga (Bhubaneswar) turnaround: occupancy 50% and ARPOB ₹35k today; management targets 50-80% higher on both within ~12 months.
Acquisitions (management is comfortable at up to 2.5x net debt/EBITDA) and the medical-college plan (~₹300 cr per college).

sections.title: Big-city tertiary and quaternary hospitals: transplants, cancer, cardiac and neuro care, mostly in Delhi NCR

blocks.p: Max runs large multi-specialty hospitals that treat complex cases: ~4,700 liver and ~6,000 kidney transplants and ~2,300 bone-marrow transplants to date, a cancer franchise that was a quarter of inpatient revenue until 2025, robotic surgery (18 robots) and cardiac, neuro and orthopaedic programmes. Of its 5,379 operational beds at Jun-2026, 2,548 are in Delhi NCR (Saket, BLK-Max, Patparganj, Shalimar Bagh, Dwarka, Vaishali, Noida, Panchsheel), 590 in Maharashtra (Nanavati-Max in Mumbai, Nagpur), 488 in Punjab (Mohali, Bathinda), plus Lucknow, Dehradun, Gurugram and, since May-2026, Bhubaneswar. Revenue per occupied bed-day (ARPOB) is the highest of any listed chain (₹81.9k in Q1FY27) because most beds are in rich metros with high insurance cover and many international patients (~9% of hospital revenue, ₹897 cr in FY26).

**How it is organised matters.** Max owns most hospitals through MHIL and subsidiaries, runs others under long contracts as "managed facilities" (consolidated as silos), and operates three hospitals owned by charitable societies under medical-service agreements running to 2064-2105: Max Saket East (Devki Devi Society), Max Smart (Gujarmal Modi Society) and Max Patparganj (Balaji Society). These "Partner Healthcare Facilities" (PHFs) are not consolidated, but Max reports a "Network" P&L that includes them, and most KPIs and broker estimates are on that basis. In FY26 the PHFs added ₹2,292 cr of revenue (₹638 cr of which was paid to MHIL as fees and supplies) and ₹286 cr of EBITDA. Two small businesses complete the group: Max Lab (pathology for outside patients, ₹201 cr) and Max@Home (home care, ₹263 cr gross).

sections.title: Too few good beds in rich cities, more insurance, and a building boom that raises the bar

blocks.p: India has far fewer hospital beds than the WHO's 3 per 1,000 people in Max's states: Delhi 2.2 (0.8 private), Haryana 1.4 (0.9 private), Maharashtra 1.8 (1.6), Uttar Pradesh 1.3 (1.0) (CRISIL, via Max's deck). Health-insurance premiums grew 18% a year from FY18 to FY25, and group plus individual policies now cover 58% of insured lives (35% in FY18). Metro hospitals bill more per day: on Max's comparison for Q1FY27, ARPOB was ₹82k at Max (73% of beds in metros), ₹74k at Fortis (74%), ₹70k at Medanta (50%), ₹67k at Apollo (58%), ₹53k at Narayana (68%) and ₹47k at KIMS (51%). The economics favour big-city hospitals with complex specialties: insurance and self-pay patients pay hospital tariffs, while government schemes (CGHS, ECHS, PSUs, state schemes) pay fixed package rates that Max says do not cover full costs. The risks are rising supply (every large chain is adding beds in NCR) and regulation of prices, especially drugs and consumables.

sections.title: Revenue = beds × occupancy × ARPOB: Max leads on occupancy and ARPOB; now the beds are growing

blocks.p: Hospital revenue is the product of three numbers: **operational beds**, **occupancy** (the share of beds filled each night) and **ARPOB** (average revenue per occupied bed-day; Max divides gross revenue, including outpatients and pharmacy but excluding Max Lab, by occupied bed-days). Max's occupancy has sat at 74-76% for four years, the highest among large listed chains (Apollo, Fortis 65-69%, Medanta ~62% on the company's comparison), and its ARPOB (₹77.8k in FY26, ₹81.9k in Q1FY27) is the highest. ARPOB dipped in FY25 (₹76k → ₹73.9k) because the acquired Lucknow, Nagpur and Noida hospitals bill much less, and again in Q3-Q4FY26 when high-value chemotherapy for CGHS patients stopped; excluding oncology it grew 9% in Q1FY27. EBITDA per bed, Max's favourite measure, was ₹71.7 lakh in FY26 and ₹71.2 lakh in Q1FY27.

sections.title: Who pays: insurers and self-pay patients are 70%, government schemes 21% and falling

blocks.p: Max's revenue comes from four payor groups: self-pay patients (32.5% in Q1FY27), insurance and corporates (37.8%), international patients (8.8%) and "institutional" government schemes such as CGHS, ECHS and PSU employees (20.9%, but 32% of occupied beds because they pay less per day). Management is explicit that institutional business "has never been profitable" and only absorbs fixed costs, and it is cutting that share as new beds open. The October-2025 CGHS agreement made it uneconomic to give high-value patented chemotherapy drugs to institutional patients, so Max stopped: oncology fell from 26% of inpatient revenue to 21-22%, and Network revenue growth slowed to 10% in Q4FY26. The base effect fades from Q3FY27; management expects oncology to stay at 21-22% of the mix, with other specialties filling the beds. A CGHS rate revision (~₹140 cr a year, full run-rate from June 2026) and a pre-agreed ~6% insurer price increase from Sep-Oct 2026 support FY27 pricing.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Max has a genuine moat in Delhi NCR and Mumbai: scarce land next to busy hospitals, senior clinicians in transplant, cancer, cardiac and neuro care, and a management team that has repeatedly bought weak hospitals and lifted them to network margins. The moat protects **occupancy and returns**, not **price**: government schemes, insurers and now courts set limits on what a hospital can charge, and every large competitor is adding beds in the same cities, which pushes up doctors' pay. It is a strong franchise, not a monopoly.

sections.title: Revenue up 3.3x since FY21 and EBITDA 5.5x; but profit growth lagged as depreciation and interest caught up

blocks.p: MHIL's consolidated revenue rose from ₹2,508 cr in FY21 (the first year after the Radiant merger, hit by Covid) to ₹8,373 cr in FY26, 27% a year. About a third of the FY23-26 growth was bought: the Lucknow, Nagpur and Noida hospitals (~1,300 beds) were acquired in FY25, when revenue jumped 30%. EBITDA grew faster (₹407 cr to ₹2,243 cr) as margins went from 16% to 27%. Profit is noisier: FY23 included a ₹244 cr deferred-tax gain and FY26 a ₹142 cr one-time tax gain on a subsidiary merger, so the clean trend is ₹860 cr (FY23) → ₹1,058 cr → ₹1,114 cr → ₹1,341 cr (FY26): ~16% a year, slower than EBITDA because depreciation and interest doubled after the acquisitions and new towers.

sections.title: Cash generation is strong, but capex now exceeds it and returns are falling

blocks.p: Max turns ~75% of EBITDA into operating cash (FY26: ₹1,633 cr). Until FY24 that easily covered capex. Since then the company has spent on acquisitions (~1,300 beds in FY25), brownfield towers and loans to the Max Smart society, and borrowed to do it: net debt including leases went from net cash of ₹780 cr (Mar-23) to ₹2,772 cr (Mar-26). Returns are falling as a result: the company's own pre-tax ROCE was 33% in FY23 and 21.8% in FY26 (about 31% for hospitals more than four years old), and Screener's ROCE, which counts the 2020 merger goodwill, is ~15%. The next phase is bigger: ₹6,961 cr of project outflow over FY27-30 on the company's own estimate, before land, routine capex and any acquisitions.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audits, but two sets of numbers and a string of one-offs

bullets: **Network vs consolidated.** Two sets of numbers. MHIL consolidated (Ind AS; FY26 revenue ₹8,373 cr, Screener EBITDA ₹2,243 cr, PAT ₹1,442 cr) and the 'Network' (adds the three PHF societies: FY26 net revenue ₹10,065 cr, operating EBITDA ₹2,638 cr, PAT ₹1,631 cr). The company's KPIs and most broker estimates are on the Network basis; EPS in the accounts (₹14.83) is on the consolidated basis. In FY26 the partner societies added ₹286 cr of EBITDA and ₹174 cr of profit that MHIL does not own; MHIL earns from them through fees (₹638 cr of intra-network revenue) and interest on ₹746 cr of loans.

**One-offs.** FY23: ₹244 cr deferred-tax gain (voluntary liquidation of subsidiaries). FY25: ₹74 cr YEIDA charge (Jaypee acquisition) as exceptional, ₹18 cr DTL gain. FY26: ~₹142 cr tax gain on the CRL-JHL amalgamation (Q2FY26 tax rate −10%), ₹48 cr exceptional (Labour Code, stamp duty). Reported EPS was ₹11.37 / 10.88 / 11.07 / 14.82 in FY23-26; before one-offs ₹8.9 / 10.9 / 11.5 / 13.8. We use the adjusted series for growth rates and the P/E cross-check.

**Goodwill and intangibles.** Goodwill ₹3,488 cr and other intangibles ₹2,518 cr at Mar-26 (consolidated), largely from the 2020 merger fair valuation and acquisitions: reported ROE (~14%) understates returns on cash invested; the company's own pre-tax ROCE excludes them (21.8% FY26 overall, ~31% for units over 4 years old excl. CWIP).

**Leases.** Lease liabilities ₹572 cr (consolidated) and ₹589 cr (Network) at Mar-26; EBITDA is post-Ind AS 116. Rent is small for Max (mostly owned or long-term contracted hospitals), so the pre/post Ind AS gap is ~1% of EBITDA value; asset-light built-to-suit hospitals (Mohali, Thane, Dehradun) will add lease debt as they open.

**Working capital.** Network DSO 95 days at Jun-26 (87 at Mar-26) on slow CGHS/PSU collections; consolidated receivables ₹1,049 cr at Mar-26 (₹776 cr a year earlier). Operating cash was 73% of EBITDA in FY26 (78% in FY25).

**Non-cash items below "operating EBITDA".** The company's headline EBITDA excludes ESOP cost (₹48 cr in FY26) and fair-value moves on contingent consideration owed to societies (₹10 cr gain in FY26); Screener's EBITDA (our base) is after them.
**Audit.** S.R. Batliboi & Co. LLP (EY); unqualified. The Network memorandum consolidation is certified by an independent firm but the societies' IGAAP numbers are not audited by Max's auditor.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Nothing suggests aggressive accounting, and disclosure is better than most peers (Network and consolidated, memorandum consolidation every quarter). But investors must do work to compare like with like: the company's headline EBITDA, PAT and KPIs include hospitals it does not own, tax one-offs have flattered reported EPS in two of the last four years, and merger goodwill hides the true return on capital.

sections.title: From net cash to ₹2,800 cr of net debt in three years; still under 1.3x EBITDA

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 MHIL (consolidated) had ₹2,907 cr of borrowings (term loans and an ECB, partly hedged), ₹572 cr of lease liabilities and ₹701 cr of cash and bank balances: **net debt of ₹2,772 cr including leases**, 1.2x FY26 EBITDA. In Q1FY27 the Kalinga purchase (₹298 cr, ECB-funded) and YPPL added ~₹480 cr more on the company's Network measure (₹1,908 cr → ₹2,384 cr, which excludes leases and nets the PHF societies' cash). Two other items matter: ₹746 cr of interest-bearing loans to the Gujarmal Modi society that owns Max Smart (an asset we leave out of net debt; its ₹69 cr of interest sits in other income), and ~₹6,000 cr of goodwill and intangibles from the 2020 merger and acquisitions, which inflate capital employed and depress reported ROE. CARE rates the company AA+ (Stable).

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Max Healthcare Institute (MHIL consolidated, ₹ crore, Screener basis). One reportable segment, so the engine runs on a single revenue-growth path and a post-Ind AS 116 EBITDA margin (rent is not in EBITDA; lease interest is in interest; lease liabilities sit in borrowings, so the model's net cash is net of leases). The company's KPIs are on the 'Network' basis (MHIL plus three Partner Healthcare Facility societies); the bed build in `businessLines` builds Network hospital revenue (beds x 365 x occupancy x ARPOB), adds Max Lab, converts gross to net revenue and takes MHIL's consolidated share; the authoring script checks it equals model revenue. Shares: Screener FY26 profit / EPS = 97.30 cr = actual 97.33 cr (no patch). Valued on EV/EBITDA, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: From the bed build below. FY27 +19%: Q1 consolidated revenue +16.7% (Network gross +16%, +20% excluding oncology) with Kalinga only from 18-May; Q2-Q4 get the rest of Max Smart (PHF, but Max earns service fees), the last ~50 Nanavati beds, Kalinga for a full year, +100 Lucknow beds and the first ~200 Gurugram beds from end-CY2026, the oncology base effect from Q3 and the ~6% insurer price revision from Sep-Oct. FY28 +18%: Gurugram ramp, Zirakpur Mohali (400) and Nagpur (100). FY29 +15%: Pitampura, Dehradun, Patparganj (PHF, end-FY29). Street (Network net revenue) FY27E +18.5% (PL) to +24% (MOSL).

businessLines._why: Network hospital gross revenue = average operational beds x 365 x occupancy x ARPOB (company definition: gross revenue excl. Max Lab ÷ OBDs). FY26 check: (₹10,538 cr gross - ₹201 cr Max Lab) ÷ ₹77,800 = 13.29 lakh OBDs = 4,790 average beds at 76% (Mar-25 4,654, Mar-26 4,966). FY27 5,540 average beds (Q1 implied 5,231; 5,379 at Jun-26 rising to ~5,950 by Mar-27), occupancy 74% (75% in Q1; Gurugram starts low), ARPOB ₹82,300 (+6%: Q1 ₹81.9k; oncology base effect, CGHS rate revision, insurer hikes, less ~2% dilution from Kalinga at ₹35k). FY28 6,250 beds, 73%, ₹86,500 (+5%); FY29 6,750 beds, 73.5%, ₹91,250 (+5.5%) — management: ARPOB grows a couple of points above inflation. Max Lab ₹240 / 285 / 335 cr (+18-20% a year; ₹58 cr in Q1FY27, +20%). Net/gross 0.952 (FY26 0.955, Q1FY27 0.951). MHIL's consolidated share of Network net revenue 0.835 / 0.84 / 0.84 (FY25 0.811, FY26 0.832, Q1FY27 0.835): it rises as owned units (Gurugram, Kalinga, Lucknow, Mohali, Nagpur) grow faster than the PHFs, offset by Max Smart's new tower sitting in a PHF.

assumptions._marginWhy: Consolidated EBITDA margin (Screener basis: after ESOP cost; post-Ind AS 116): 27.6% FY24, 26.3% FY25, 26.8% FY26 (Q2-Q4FY26: 26.9%, 26.0%, 28.3%), 25.3% in Q1FY27 (25.8% a year earlier) with ₹195 cr of Network overheads for new units. Management: no significant rise in indirect costs until Gurugram opens, so new-bed revenue drops through from Q2. FY27 26.4%: Q2-Q4 ~0.5pp above FY26's quarters, less Gurugram start-up costs; FY28 26.9%: brownfield towers mature, oncology normalised, offset by Gurugram, Zirakpur and Nagpur start-up losses; FY29 27.4%. Network equivalents are ~0.5-1pp lower (Network operating margin 26.2% in FY26). Street (Network): PL 26.6% / 26.6%, MOSL 25.4% / 26.4%, Antique ~27% by FY28.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY27 ₹2,300 cr = ₹386 cr paid for Kalinga and YPPL in Q1 + ₹1,711 cr of project outflow (company estimate for FY27) + ~₹200 cr routine capex. FY28 ₹3,010 cr = ₹2,340 cr project outflow + ₹220 cr routine + ~₹450 cr of new lease liabilities for the 400-bed built-to-suit Zirakpur, Mohali hospital (GAM estimate from Dwarka: lease liabilities rose ₹372 cr in FY25 for ~300 beds). FY29 ₹2,565 cr = ₹2,025 cr + ₹240 cr routine + ~₹300 cr of leases (Pitampura, Dehradun). Project outflow (deck, 17-Aug-2026) excludes land and the medical-college plan (~₹300 cr per college, not firmed); it includes the funding of PHF projects (Max Smart, Patparganj), which Max lends to the societies at ~9.25% — we treat it all as capex (cash-conservative; the engine has no separate loan asset). New leases are added because lease liabilities count as debt in the model.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹447 cr = 3.1% of average gross block (₹14,232 cr, which includes ~₹6,000 cr of goodwill-like merger intangibles that are barely amortised); Q1FY27 ₹132 cr (₹528 cr annualised) after Mohali, Nanavati and Lucknow capitalisation. 3.4% gives FY27E ~₹553 cr. The engine depreciates capex at once while projects sit in CWIP (₹592 cr at Mar-26).
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Zero because the engine applies the yield to net cash after borrowings and lease liabilities, which is negative (net debt ₹2,812 cr at Mar-26). Interest income is built in `otherIncome` instead.

otherIncomeBuild._why: Built from AR FY26 note 28 (consolidated other income ₹162.6 cr; ₹155.6 cr in FY25). Treasury: bank-deposit interest ₹29.6 cr (FY25 ₹53.1 cr) on ~₹690 cr average cash (4.3%); we take 4.5% on ₹600 / 500 / 450 cr of average cash as capex absorbs cash. Loans to PHFs (₹746 cr at Mar-26 to Gujarmal Modi Hospital for Max Smart, 9.25%): ₹68.6 cr in FY26; ~₹800 / 900 / 1,000 cr average loans at 9.25% as Smart and Patparganj are funded. Recurring other (₹58 cr in FY26, ₹62 cr in FY25): unwinding on long-dated receivables and deposits ~₹11 cr, write-backs of unclaimed balances ₹24-31 cr a year (we take ~₹28 cr), deferred EPCG credit, tax-refund interest and others ~₹16-18 cr: ₹55 / 56 / 57 cr. Left out as one-offs: fair-value gain on contingent consideration ₹5.1 cr, asset-sale gain, lease modification. FY27E ₹156 cr vs FY26 ₹162.6 cr and ₹166.6 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26 (before exceptional items): lower deposit interest as cash funds Kalinga and projects.

assumptions._interestLabel: Finance cost (borrowings + lease interest; gross, before interest income)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹235 cr (incl. ₹54 cr of lease interest); Q1FY27 ₹71 cr (₹284 cr annualised) after the ECB for Kalinga. Gross debt rises with ~₹7,900 cr of capex and leases over FY27-29 against ~₹7,500 cr of operating cash; interest on ~8% of average borrowings plus lease interest (~9.5%) and less capitalisation as projects complete: ₹300 / 360 / 400 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax plus minorities (the engine has no minority line). The enacted rate is 25.17%; profits of the managed facilities (silos) are not taxed at MHIL, worth ~2.4pp in FY26 (AR FY26 tax reconciliation: ₹40 cr on ₹1,676 cr PBT). FY26 underlying 22.4% (₹233 cr reported plus the ₹142 cr one-time amalgamation gain); FY25 23.5%; but Q4FY26 26.4% and Q1FY27 26.0% (MHIL). We use 24.5%, incl. ~0.3pp for minorities (41.72% of Kalinga, ~49.78% of YPPL, both small). Brokers use 20-23% on the Network, where the PHF societies pay little tax.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividends: ₹1.5 a share for FY25 (₹146 cr), ₹2 recommended for FY26 (~13% of profit).

dcf._betaWhy: Ke = 6.5% + 0.85 x 6% = 11.6%. Net debt incl. leases is ~3% of enterprise value, so WACC is ~11.4%; the engine discounts at the cost of equity, which we keep (slightly conservative). Defensive demand; regulatory and expansion risk.
dcf._tgWhy: 6%: bed density in North India is well below the WHO norm and ARPOB grows above inflation, but supply is rising fast in NCR.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~15% (FY29E) to 9% by year 15 as the ~10,000-bed network matures.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 27.5% consolidated (FY24 27.6%, FY26 26.8%): new hospitals mature, but more beds sit in lower-ARPOB cities (Lucknow, Nagpur, Bhubaneswar) and doctor costs rise.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex incl. leases falls from ~19-26% of revenue (expansion) to 9%: replacement (depreciation ~5.5% of revenue) plus growth capex for ~9% growth via brownfields.

No growth adjustment: EBITDA growth slows from 22% a year (FY23-26, with acquisitions) to ~18% (FY26-29E) while capex doubles. Bull 37.5x and bear 26x = the 75th and 25th percentiles of the same history (40.3x, 28.2x) after the same de-rating.

Bull 60x, bear 42x scale with the EV/EBITDA multiples.
